acceptance: Mutations and reads do not block on synchronous full repack when slack crosses HARD_SLACK_CAP_BYTES.
Heavy write bursts degrade gracefully via an incremental or tiered compaction strategy without unbounded latency spikes.
context: Identified in Muse review of 0.10.0/0.10.1 maintenance triggers. HARD_SLACK_CAP_BYTES (16 MiB) triggers synchronous inline maintain() under LOCK_EX.
description: When unpacked slack exceeds the 16 MiB HARD_SLACK_CAP_BYTES, maybe_maintain() executes maintain() synchronously inline rather than via detached background process. On large repositories (like BenchBox with 5,100+ commits), this causes a synchronous repack -A + prune run inside the caller's mutation or fetch (holding LOCK_EX for ~0.6-2s), introducing a latency spike for that specific request. A tiered or incremental compaction ladder would prevent this latency cliff.
